instruction: Start GIMP from the terminal to edit "cola.png" and trim the left 30% from the image, then export as "cropped.png".

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires cropping left 30% of cola.png (1233x1280). Expected result: 863x1280. Verified: 1233 * 0.7 = 863 pixels width (rounded).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator only checks output dimensions (863x1280) but not which portion of the image was cropped
Cannot distinguish between cropping left 30% vs right 30% vs other 30% - all would pass if dimensions match
The instruction explicitly requires 'trim the left 30%' but this directional requirement is unverifiable with dimension-only checking
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add visual content verification by comparing cropped image against a reference (e.g., check if right edge pixels match original right edge pixels)
Use perceptual hash or image similarity metrics to verify the correct portion of the image was kept
Add a getter that extracts and compares specific pixel regions from both original and cropped images to verify correct side was trimmed
Alternatively, simplify instruction to 'crop to 863x1280' without specifying direction (though this reduces task precision)
